top.headline: Eagles erase 21-point deficit, stun Cowboys 39-38
top.summary: Joe Milton and DeVonta Smith (11 catches, 200 yards, 2 TD) led Philadelphia back from 31-10 down, and Jake Elliott won it with a 59-yard field goal with 2 seconds left. It was the biggest comeback in Thanksgiving history. The Eagles move to 4-7; Dallas falls to 5-7.

top.headline: Bears beat Lions 39-35 on a TD with 3 seconds left, take NFC North lead
top.summary: Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for the winning touchdown with 3 seconds left in a shootout at Ford Field. Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 205 yards and three touchdowns for Detroit. Chicago's sixth straight win puts it at 9-2, alone in first in the NFC North; Detroit is 8-3.

top.headline: Bass hits 57-yarder at the buzzer as Bills edge Chiefs 13-10
top.summary: Tyler Bass kicked a 57-yard field goal as time expired in the rain at Highmark Stadium. Buffalo won despite Josh Allen going 10-of-21 for 81 yards with two interceptions. The Bills (10-1) are the first team to 10 wins and have won seven straight; the Chiefs (8-3) trail Denver in the AFC West.

leagues.summary: Three last-second Thanksgiving finishes: Eagles erase 21 in Dallas, Bears take the NFC North lead, Bills first to 10 wins

stories.headline: Aaron Rodgers clears waivers, becomes a free agent
stories.summary: No team claimed Rodgers before Thursday's 4 p.m. ET deadline, a day after Pittsburgh released him. ESPN reported no teams showing interest so far. Mason Rudolph starts for the Steelers against the Broncos on Friday.

standouts.name: DeVonta Smith
standouts.note: Touchdown catches of 50 and 45 yards in the record comeback.

standouts.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
standouts.note: His 70-yard touchdown run gave Detroit a late lead before Chicago's last-second winner.

standouts.name: Joe Milton
standouts.note: Also ran for two touchdowns as Philadelphia came back from 21 down.

leagues.name: NBA
leagues.summary: No games on Thanksgiving; Haliburton and Jaylen Brown out, LaMelo Ball questionable for Friday's 11-game Cup finale

stories.headline: Black Friday: 11 games close NBA Cup group play
stories.summary: The NBA took Thanksgiving off and returns Friday with 11 games that finish group play, led by Heat at Knicks (7 ET) and Lakers at Spurs (9:30 ET). In West Group C, the Spurs, Blazers, Warriors and Lakers can all still win the group. Orlando, Detroit and Toronto are bunched in East Group A.

stories.headline: Jaylen Brown out at Indiana; Embiid questionable as Sixers chase Cup berth
stories.summary: The 76ers ruled Brown out for Friday's game at Indiana with his left hamstring. Joel Embiid, who has missed two games with an illness, is questionable. A win clinches East Group B and sends Philadelphia to the knockout round for the first time.

stories.headline: Haliburton ruled out for Friday despite hoping to return
stories.summary: Tyrese Haliburton is listed as out for Friday's Cup game against the 76ers. He said Wednesday he hoped to return within the week. He has been out with a left hamstring strain since Oct. 26.

stories.headline: LaMelo Ball questionable for Wolves' Cup decider vs. Memphis
stories.summary: Minnesota listed Ball as questionable for Friday with a left ankle sprain after he left Wednesday's win in Oklahoma City. The 3-0 Wolves host Memphis with a Cup berth on the line.

stories.headline: Knicks' Anunoby doubtful; Pistons' Cunningham out Friday
stories.summary: OG Anunoby (left calf strain) is doubtful against Miami and would miss a fourth straight game. Cade Cunningham misses a second straight game with right knee tendinopathy. Memphis lists Zach Edey (left ankle) as questionable at Minnesota.

moves.text: Pistons: Cade Cunningham (right knee tendinopathy) out Friday vs. Bucks
Grizzlies: Zach Edey (left ankle) and Isaiah Stewart (right hip) questionable Friday at Minnesota
Pacers: Aaron Nesmith off the injury report; T.J. McConnell, Kelly Oubre Jr. and Larry Nance Jr. questionable
Trail Blazers: Ja Morant (left hamstring) has resumed five-on-five work and could return on the home stand

leagues.name: NHL
leagues.summary: No games on Thanksgiving; Devils' Brenden Dillon gets four games for a hit on Denton Mateychuk

stories.headline: Devils' Brenden Dillon suspended four games
stories.summary: The NHL suspended Dillon four games for an illegal check to the head that injured Columbus defenseman Denton Mateychuk in Wednesday's shootout game. Dillon got a match penalty on the play. He forfeits $82,474.24.

stories.headline: Kantserov keeps scoring for Blackhawks
stories.summary: Roman Kantserov scored twice in Seattle as Chicago won its third straight road game. He has 15 goals and 20 points in 25 games and leads all rookies in both. He's the first Blackhawks skater with 15 goals through his first 25 games since Bill Mosienko.

stories.headline: Goals at a record pace by Thanksgiving
stories.summary: Teams have scored 2,546 goals so far in 2026-27, the most in league history before U.S. Thanksgiving. That's more than 150 above the next closest season, 2019-20 (2,380).

stories.headline: Thanksgiving playoff picture: Canadiens look vulnerable
stories.summary: Teams in a playoff spot at U.S. Thanksgiving have about a 75 percent chance of staying there, per Sportsnet. Montreal holds a spot but has a minus-one goal differential and a three-game losing streak. Minnesota sets the pace in the Central.

leagues.name: MLB
leagues.summary: Offseason · quiet Thanksgiving; Suzuki reportedly wants more than $120M before Tuesday's lockout deadline

stories.headline: Seiya Suzuki reportedly seeking more than $120M
stories.summary: The New York Post's Jon Heyman reports Suzuki wants more than the six-year, $120MM deal Teruaki Sato got from the Cubs, and figures Randy Arozarena's ask is in the same range. The Blue Jays, Padres and Phillies have been linked to both. Both want to sign before a lockout can begin at 11:59 p.m. ET Tuesday.

stories.headline: Orioles reportedly willing to trade infielders for starting pitching
stories.summary: Baltimore has told teams it will deal from its surplus of third basemen to add starters, per The Athletic and the New York Post. Joel Sherman names Blaze Alexander, Christian Encarnacion-Strand, Coby Mayo and Jordan Westburg. The Orioles already added Freddy Peralta.

stories.headline: Yankees show interest in lefty Alex Vesia
stories.summary: The Athletic reports the Yankees have interest in the free-agent reliever and also want a right-handed-hitting catcher. Vesia has also been linked to the Mariners, Blue Jays, Mets and Marlins and reportedly wants three years.

stories.headline: Marlins drawing trade interest in Kyle Stowers
stories.summary: The Miami Herald's Barry Jackson writes that Miami is in trade talks and Stowers is drawing interest. He enters his first year of arbitration with three years of control left.
